newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW says will create 400 temporary jobs.
newsitem.headline: VW says will create 400 temporary jobs.

text.p: Volkswagen AG and engineering union IG Metall on Wednesday adjourned wage talks but the carmaker said it had agreed to hire 400 new employees on a temporary basis at 10 percent less pay than average.
In a statement released after the fourth round of wage talks for VW's 90,000 employees in west Germany, the company said the jobs would last at least six months and up to 18 months.
Volkswagen had earlier said strong demand for the new version of its Passat saloon may mean adding about 400 jobs at its plant in Emden.
While VW's works council was seeking at least 1,000 new posts, the union said the 400 new jobs were a success in the fight against unemployment.
A fifth round of wage talks will be held on May 15 and May 16.
The temporary workers will earn about 400 marks less per month than other VW employees.
IG Metall's chief negotiator in the talks, Juergen Peters, said the union had succeeded in pushing through the creation of new jobs and the cut in pay was justified for the sake of a compromise.

He said it could not be ruled out that the temporary jobs could become permanent if the economy developed well. Overall the new jobs showed that VW's system of a four-day week was conducive to creating new jobs.
